title: Creatures of the deep
paragraphs: The ocean covers over 70% of the surface of our planet, though, according to the National Ocean Service, 95% of it remains unexplored. This is because under the surface is a dark and hostile environment with unrelenting high pressure, freezing temperatures and bizarre creatures in the depths.

The Census of Marine Life reports more than 17,000 species living in the deep sea. The Greenland shark can live in depths of 7,200 feet and is a rarely seen Arctic predator said to live to 400 years old and reach 23 feet in length. In order to battle the icy depths, Greenland sharks have chemicals in their skin which prevent ice crystals from forming on their body.

Another deep-sea creature is the giant squid, an animal that remains a mystery to scientists despite being the largest invertebrate on Earth. Living far below the surface, what we know has largely come from carcasses being washed ashore. Marine biologists have found that they feed on fish, squid and possibly even small whales. They find prey using eyes which are ten inches wide, roughly the size of a dinner plate!

Other unusual creatures include the vampire squid, which lives 2000 to 3000 feet under the ocean and is so-called because of its dark cloak that connects its eight arms. There is also the dumbo octopus, named due to its resemblance to the elephant from the 1943 Disney film Dumbo, with its protruding ears. Another unique creature is the anglerfish known for the light that hangs from its head.
So, enjoy swimming, but don’t venture too far down – you never know what is lurking beneath!

vocabulary.entry: unexplored /ˌʌnɪkˈsplɔːd/ adj. 未被探索的；未开发的
vocabulary.example: Large areas of the rainforest remain unexplored.
vocabulary.translation: 热带雨林的大片区域仍未被探索。

vocabulary.entry: hostile /ˈhɒstaɪl/ adj. （环境）恶劣的；充满敌意的；敌对的
vocabulary.example: The team faced a hostile environment in the desert.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍在沙漠中遭遇了恶劣的环境。

vocabulary.entry: unrelenting /ʌnrɪˈlentɪŋ/ adj. 持续不断的；不松懈的；无情的
vocabulary.example: We struggled against the unrelenting wind all day.
vocabulary.translation: 我们一整天都在和持续不断的大风抗争。

vocabulary.entry: freezing /ˈfriːzɪŋ/ adj. 极冷的；冰冻的
vocabulary.example: The temperature dropped to freezing last night.
vocabulary.translation: 昨晚气温降到了冰点。

vocabulary.entry: bizarre /bɪˈzɑː(r)/ adj. 奇异的；古怪的；怪诞的
vocabulary.example: She told a bizarre story about her trip to the mountains.
vocabulary.translation: 她讲了一个关于她登山之旅的离奇故事。

vocabulary.entry: depth /depθ/ n. 深处；深海；深渊
vocabulary.example: The diver descended to a depth of 50 metres.
vocabulary.translation: 潜水员下潜到了50米的深海处。

vocabulary.entry: Census of Marine Life /ˈsensəs ɒv məˈriːn laɪf/ n. 海洋生物普查
vocabulary.example: The Census of Marine Life has discovered thousands of new sea species.
vocabulary.translation: 海洋生物普查已经发现了数千种新的海洋物种。

vocabulary.entry: species /ˈspiːʃiːz/ n. 物种；种类
vocabulary.example: This rare species of bird is found only in the Amazon.
vocabulary.translation: 这种珍稀鸟类只在亚马逊地区被发现。

vocabulary.entry: Greenland shark /ˈɡriːnlænd ʃɑːk/ n. 格陵兰睡鲨
vocabulary.example: The Greenland shark is one of the longest-living vertebrates on Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 格陵兰睡鲨是地球上寿命最长的脊椎动物之一。

vocabulary.entry: Arctic /ˈɑːktɪk/ adj. 北极的；北冰洋的 n. 北极地区
vocabulary.example: Polar bears live in the Arctic region.
vocabulary.translation: 北极熊生活在北极地区。

vocabulary.entry: predator /ˈpredətə(r)/ n. 捕食者；食肉动物
vocabulary.example: Lions are top predators in the African savanna.
vocabulary.translation: 狮子是非洲稀树草原上的顶级捕食者。

vocabulary.entry: length /leŋθ/ n. 身长；长度；持续时间
vocabulary.example: The snake can reach a length of two metres.
vocabulary.translation: 这种蛇的身长可达两米。

vocabulary.entry: battle /ˈbætl/ v. 对抗；搏斗；作战 n. 战斗；战役
vocabulary.example: The plant battles against the harsh sun to survive.
vocabulary.translation: 这种植物为了生存对抗着强烈的阳光。

vocabulary.entry: icy /ˈaɪsi/ adj. 冰冷的；结满冰的
vocabulary.example: We had to walk on the icy road with great care.
vocabulary.translation: 我们不得不小心翼翼地走在结冰的路上。

vocabulary.entry: chemical /ˈkemɪkl/ n. 化学物质 adj. 化学的
vocabulary.example: The plant produces a special chemical to protect itself from insects.
vocabulary.translation: 这种植物会产生一种特殊的化学物质来保护自己免受昆虫侵害。

vocabulary.entry: crystal /ˈkrɪstl/ n. 晶体；水晶
vocabulary.example: Salt crystals form when the water evaporates.
vocabulary.translation: 水分蒸发后会形成盐晶体。

vocabulary.entry: giant squid /ˈdʒaɪənt skwɪd/ n. 大王乌贼
vocabulary.example: The giant squid is one of the most mysterious sea creatures.
vocabulary.translation: 大王乌贼是最神秘的海洋生物之一。

vocabulary.entry: mystery /ˈmɪstəri/ n. 谜；神秘的事物；奥秘
vocabulary.example: The origin of the ancient monument remains a mystery.
vocabulary.translation: 这座古老遗迹的起源仍是一个谜。

vocabulary.entry: invertebrate /ɪnˈvɜːtɪbrət/ n. 无脊椎动物 adj. 无脊椎的
vocabulary.example: Jellyfish and squid are both invertebrates.
vocabulary.translation: 水母和乌贼都是无脊椎动物。

vocabulary.entry: carcass /ˈkɑːkəs/ n. 动物尸体；躯体
vocabulary.example: The beach was closed after a whale carcass was washed ashore.
vocabulary.translation: 一头鲸鱼的尸体被冲上岸后，这片海滩就关闭了。

vocabulary.entry: wash ashore /wɒʃ əˈʃɔː(r)/ 被冲上岸；冲至岸边
vocabulary.example: Hundreds of plastic bottles are washed ashore every day on this beach.
vocabulary.translation: 每天有数百个塑料瓶被冲上这片海滩。

vocabulary.entry: marine biologist /məˈriːn baɪˈɒlədʒɪst/ n. 海洋生物学家
vocabulary.example: The marine biologist spent years studying coral reefs.
vocabulary.translation: 这位海洋生物学家花了数年时间研究珊瑚礁。

vocabulary.entry: feed on /fiːd ɒn/ 以……为食；吃……
vocabulary.example: Owls feed on mice and other small animals.
vocabulary.translation: 猫头鹰以老鼠和其他小动物为食。

vocabulary.entry: prey /preɪ/ n. 猎物；牺牲品 v. 捕食
vocabulary.example: The eagle circled the sky looking for prey.
vocabulary.translation: 老鹰在天空盘旋，寻找猎物。

vocabulary.entry: roughly /ˈrʌfli/ adv. 大约；大致；粗略地
vocabulary.example: The project will take roughly three months to complete.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目大约需要三个月完成。

vocabulary.entry: dinner plate /ˈdɪnə pleɪt/ n. 餐盘；正餐盘
vocabulary.example: She placed the steak on a large dinner plate.
vocabulary.translation: 她把牛排放在一个大盘子里。

vocabulary.entry: vampire squid /ˈvæmpaɪə skwɪd/ n. 吸血鬼乌贼
vocabulary.example: The vampire squid lives in the dark deep sea and has a unique appearance.
vocabulary.translation: 吸血鬼乌贼生活在黑暗的深海中，外形十分独特。

vocabulary.entry: cloak /kləʊk/ n. 斗篷；遮盖物 v. 遮盖
vocabulary.example: The bird has a dark cloak of feathers on its back.
vocabulary.translation: 这种鸟的背部有一层深色的羽毛“斗篷”。

vocabulary.entry: dumbo octopus /ˈdʌmbə ˈɒktəpəs/ n. 小飞象章鱼
vocabulary.example: The dumbo octopus gets its name from its ear-like fins.
vocabulary.translation: 小飞象章鱼因其形似耳朵的鳍而得名。

vocabulary.entry: resemblance /rɪˈzembləns/ n. 相似；相像
vocabulary.example: There is a strong resemblance between the mother and her daughter.
vocabulary.translation: 这位母亲和她的女儿长得非常像。

vocabulary.entry: protruding /prəˈtruːdɪŋ/ adj. 突出的；伸出的
vocabulary.example: The animal has two protruding eyes on the top of its head.
vocabulary.translation: 这种动物的头顶有两只突出的眼睛。

vocabulary.entry: anglerfish /ˈæŋɡləfɪʃ/ n. 琵琶鱼；安康鱼
vocabulary.example: The anglerfish uses the light on its head to attract prey in the dark sea.
vocabulary.translation: 琵琶鱼用头部的光在黑暗的海洋中吸引猎物。

vocabulary.entry: venture /ˈventʃə(r)/ v. 冒险前往；大胆尝试 n. 冒险；风险
vocabulary.example: We decided not to venture into the forest at night.
vocabulary.translation: 我们决定不冒险在晚上进入森林。

vocabulary.entry: lurk /lɜːk/ v. 潜伏；隐藏；暗藏
vocabulary.example: Danger may lurk in the dark corners of the old building.
vocabulary.translation: 这座老建筑的黑暗角落里可能暗藏危险。

vocabulary.entry: beneath /bɪˈniːθ/ prep. 在……之下；低于 adv. 在下方
vocabulary.example: The treasure lies beneath the old tree.
vocabulary.translation: 宝藏藏在那棵老树的下方。

sentences.english: The ocean covers over 70% of the surface of our planet, though, according to the National Ocean Service, 95% of it remains unexplored.
sentences.chinese: 海洋覆盖了地球表面70%以上的区域，但据美国国家海洋和大气管理局称，其中95%的海域仍未被人类探索。

sentences.english: This is because under the surface is a dark and hostile environment with unrelenting high pressure, freezing temperatures and bizarre creatures in the depths.
sentences.chinese: 这是因为海面之下是一个黑暗而恶劣的环境，有着持续的高压、严寒的温度，还有生活在深海里的奇异生物。

sentences.english: The Census of Marine Life reports more than 17,000 species living in the deep sea.
sentences.chinese: 海洋生物普查报告显示，深海中生活着超过17000个物种。

sentences.english: The Greenland shark can live in depths of 7,200 feet and is a rarely seen Arctic predator said to live to 400 years old and reach 23 feet in length.
sentences.chinese: 格陵兰睡鲨可以栖息在7200英尺的深海，这种罕见的北极捕食者据说能活到400岁，体长可达23英尺。

sentences.english: In order to battle the icy depths, Greenland sharks have chemicals in their skin which prevent ice crystals from forming on their body.
sentences.chinese: 为了抵御深海的严寒，格陵兰睡鲨的皮肤中含有特殊化学物质，能防止冰晶在身体表面形成。

sentences.english: Another deep-sea creature is the giant squid, an animal that remains a mystery to scientists despite being the largest invertebrate on Earth.
sentences.chinese: 另一种深海生物是大王乌贼，它是地球上体型最大的无脊椎动物，但对科学家来说，它至今仍是一个谜。

sentences.english: Living far below the surface, what we know has largely come from carcasses being washed ashore.
sentences.chinese: 大王乌贼生活在海洋深处，我们对它的了解大多来自被冲上岸的尸体。

sentences.english: Marine biologists have found that they feed on fish, squid and possibly even small whales.
sentences.chinese: 海洋生物学家发现，它们以鱼类、乌贼甚至小型鲸鱼为食。

sentences.english: They find prey using eyes which are ten inches wide, roughly the size of a dinner plate!
sentences.chinese: 它们依靠直径达10英寸的眼睛寻找猎物，那尺寸差不多相当于一个餐盘！

sentences.english: Other unusual creatures include the vampire squid, which lives 2000 to 3000 feet under the ocean and is so-called because of its dark cloak that connects its eight arms.
sentences.chinese: 其他奇特的生物还包括吸血鬼乌贼，它们生活在2000到3000英尺的深海，得名于连接着八条腕足的深色“斗篷”状皮肤。

sentences.english: There is also the dumbo octopus, named due to its resemblance to the elephant from the 1943 Disney film Dumbo, with its protruding ears.
sentences.chinese: 还有小飞象章鱼，它的名字源于1943年迪士尼动画电影《小飞象》里的大象，因为它长着一对突出的“耳朵”。

sentences.english: Another unique creature is the anglerfish known for the light that hangs from its head.
sentences.chinese: 另外一种独特的生物是琵琶鱼，它因头部悬挂着一个发光器官而闻名。

sentences.english: So, enjoy swimming, but don’t venture too far down – you never know what is lurking beneath!
sentences.chinese: 所以，尽情享受游泳的乐趣吧，但不要冒险潜得太深——你永远不知道海底深处潜伏着什么生物！
